newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kuehne says direct sell airlines will fail.
newsitem.headline: Kuehne says direct sell airlines will fail.

text.p: Airlines or other transport carriers who try to cut out freight forwarders and sell direct to shippers are doomed to failure, a top forwarder said.

Cornelius Geber, Kuehne & Nagel International AG vice-president sales and marketing and chairman of the Germany subsidiary, called on carriers to work more closely in partnership with forwarders instead.

"Those carriers, whether air, ocean, land or rail, who try for direct client contacts and bypass forwarders will not succeed because the forwarder as a multi-modal broker understands clients the best," he said in a Reuters interview.
Individual airlines or shipping companies were not in a position to provide multi-modal services, he added.
Kuehne & Nagel wanted long-term partnerships with transport suppliers in order to provide client-orientated, multi-modal "integrated logistics", he said.
"Preferred partners are those we can work globally with and there are about ten of them," Geber said.
As the biggest global ocean freight forwarder, KN worked closely with a handful of shipping companies such as Hapag-Lloyd AG.
"In airfreight co-operation between airlines and forwarders is not so close. We must be careful about direct marketing," Geber said.

"We must come to a new strategic partnership between airline and forwarder. The airlines must recognise more than at present who plays a vital role in filling their belly or freighter capacity," he added.
KN was normally very constant with its partners and did not change them unless there were exceptional circumstances as in the case of KLM Royal Dutch Airlines.
KN had decided to drop KLM as a preferred partner and had reduced its air cargo volumes with the airline substantially due to its direct sales policy.
But Geber said: "We do not think KLM will be successful long-term. They do not have the market presence and we think KLM will eventually have to find a middle way.
Air cargo fuel surcharges which had caused problems with clients were an example of the need for closer co-operation between airlines and forwarders, Geber said.
"This short-termism, erratic surcharges and the lack of a long-term rates policy always leads to frustration," he pointed out.
Close co-operation with preferred partners such as Lufthansa Cargo AG was necessary but also specific client solutions including charter operations to provide necessary capacity.

"There is a trend towards own charter operations where we as the forwarder become like an airline, especially for time-volume contracts," he said. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
